name: blueprint/heartbeat
description: The uptime pattern generalized: rh_run performs a check, the store keeps one receipt per run, success-rate is a scan, and rh_notify_send interrupts you when N checks in a row fail. Escalation is Cloudflare cron (documented, not built).
use_cases: ping me when it has been down 3 times
ingredients: rh_run (collect mode: exit code + bounded stdout/stderr - live-verified)
rh_store receipts under uptime:<ts> or smoke:<service>:<ts>
rh_run_bg for checks that must not block the turn
recipe: check: rh_run curl -sI (or any probe command) -> receipt: rh_store_put { ok: exitCode === 0, ms, at } -> scan: rh_store_list uptime:* + get the last N -> aggregate the success rate -> alert: when the last N consecutive receipts are failures, rh_notify_send once (record the sent alert so it is not repeated)
result_kind: one receipt per check + one alert per failure streak

config_variants.cadence: on-demand (agent runs the check) | cron escalation
config_variants.alert: none | notify on streak | notify on every failure

pitfalls: rh_run is collect mode and bounded - keep probe output small (headers, not bodies)
rh_run_bg reports status/exit but NOT captured stdout (live-verified) - use rh_run when the answer is the output
alert-once needs its own record (alert:uptime:<ts>): without it every turn re-alerts
exit codes and stderr surface exactly as the command produced them - a curl timeout is exit 28, not a thrown error
argv arrays only - no shell pipes; curl -sI and curl -sf are the shell-free forms
local_limits: checks only run on turns the agent actually runs
cloud_limits: cron escalation needs a Worker + the user's Cloudflare account; not a built primitive
